metadata.title: An International Perspective on Digital Literacy

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an ICILS 2023 international report/book-chapter set describing assessment design, achievement scales, and descriptive/associational results (e.g., achievement distributions and achievement gaps) rather than training/evaluating machine-learning prediction models. The ICILS sampling design is described as a two-stage cluster sample (schools selected with probability proportional to size; one class randomly sampled within each school; all students in the sampled class invited), and participation requirements are used to determine which countries’ results are reported in the main tables. The provided text does not specify the application of student/sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife) in the analyses shown here. Because no ML modeling pipeline is reported, and because the manuscript does not document explicit weight variables or replicate procedures, weighting cannot be confirmed from the excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are used for CIL and CT proficiency estimation under a rotated test booklet design, but the excerpt does not report the specific missing-data strategy for questionnaire/test data (e.g., whether missing responses were handled via listwise deletion, multiple imputation, or other procedures). Given that ICILS uses PV methods for achievement estimation, missingness handling for the underlying item/questionnaire responses is a methodological detail that is not documented in the provided text, representing a reporting gap for transparency.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: ICILS 2023 targets grade 8 students (about age 14) with an average age at least 13.5 years. The student sample is drawn via a two-stage cluster design: schools are sampled with probability proportional to size; within each sampled school, one class is randomly sampled and all students in that class are invited. Countries are included in main reporting only if they meet sampling participation requirements (85% of selected schools and 85% of selected students within participating schools, or a weighted overall participation rate of 75%); countries with overall sampling participation <50% are excluded from relevant main tables. Students are excluded if they have less than 1 year of instruction in the language of testing (including potential exclusion of Ukrainian refugee students), and Romania is excluded from some comparisons due to late testing. For CT, only countries participating in the optional CT assessment are included, and CT completion is conditional on completing the CIL test and student questionnaire.

data.outcome_summary: This ICILS 2023 report set (grade 8) provides descriptive and gap analyses for computer and information literacy (CIL) and computational thinking (CT) using PV-based proficiency estimation under a rotated test booklet design. It reports substantial cross-country variation in average CIL and CT, with CIL generally showing less within-country spread than CT. The report documents achievement gaps by gender, immigrant background, language spoken at home, socioeconomic status (parental education/occupation and books at home), and home ICT access (e.g., PC availability when needed, internet disruptions, and number of home PC devices). It also reports trends across cycles: CIL is typically lower in 2023 than in 2018/2013 in countries with comparable data, while CT changes are smaller and often not statistically significant. Finally, it quantifies the CIL–CT association using PVs, reporting an average within-country correlation of 0.76, and notes only slight changes in this association between 2018 and 2023. No machine-learning predictive modeling is evaluated in the provided text.
